contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #105: Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games.

Resolve Proposition prop:upper for every permitted parameter: legal joint partition labels, frozen usefulness marks, observations that forget the path below the upper cut, and a hidden-bucket law determined by the right input alone. The target is this local upper-decoder interface, not the entire 2-to-1 hardness theorem.

definitions.frozen: The mark U(P,bar M) is computed once under the modified lower-cut law and is not recomputed under another law.
definitions.hidden-law: The conditional hidden-bucket law after the joint analytical exposure must be the same law mu_R computable from the right input.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 105 (Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games.; papers: Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/105.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Under every stated hypothesis of Proposition prop:upper, its prescribed local strategies have agreement at least b * 2^(-ell) * tau^2/2 * 2^(-r), and every left output is a normalized product form whose displayed lower-row matrix has rank at most one. The bound is independent of lower row count, source alphabet, branching, and instance size.

The events in lem:useful-equality and lem:positive-difference are functions of the permitted upper-cut record and independent auxiliary randomness: P contains no selected descendant tag, all lower descendant outputs are retained, and usefulness marks and advice predicates are frozen.

In the modified lower-cut experiment the conditional law of X after the complete joint exposure D is exactly mu_R, a function of the right input alone, with unconditional nonzero-character biases at most (7/8)^R_j; neither the missing lower row nor the original projected questions are needed by the right decoder.

The finite-range partial-table inverse theorem and its many-good-row-fibers consequence in Section 01 apply uniformly in quotient column dimension and table range, with constants alpha,r,ell_0 depending only on the equality threshold.

For every finite binary W,H and lambda-biased law on W tensor H, the heavy lists of lem:heavy-list have at most 2/tau^2 elements and capture every compatible affine-slice predictor under exactly its stated hypotheses, using unconditional correlations under that same law.

The same local strategies in prop:upper have the stronger all-parameter lower bound b * tau^2/2 * 2^(-r), removing its explicit factor 2^(-ell): per exposure the proportion of nonannihilating output characters with conditional correlation at least rho/2 is at least p_D(q_D-rho), so their average is at least b.

For arbitrary finite character and exposure sets, bounded correlations, a nonnegative threshold, bad-character mass plus threshold at most rho, and slice probability p in [0,1], the productive-character fraction dominates p(q-rho). Nonnegative weighted averaging then preserves the positive excess b in the decoder bound b*hit. Main.lean additionally verifies the exact two-response, TV-budget, slice-mass, Gram-list and bit-bias inequalities, with their displayed hypotheses.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace UpperDecoder

theorem two_response_fiber (a b : ℝ) :
    (a + b) ^ 2 / 2 ≤ a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 := by
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b)]

theorem slice_mass (p h u lam : ℝ)
    (hp : u - lam ≤ p) (hu : h ≤ u) (hlam : lam ≤ h / 2) :
    h / 2 ≤ p := by
  linarith

theorem positive_difference (k alpha q h v : ℝ)
    (hk : 0 ≤ k) (ha : 0 ≤ alpha) (ha1 : alpha ≤ 1)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hh : q ≤ h) (hv : v ≤ alpha * q / 16) :
    k * alpha * q / 4 ≤
      (k * alpha - k * alpha / 4) * h - (k + k * alpha / 4) * v := by
  have hmargin :
      0 ≤ (3 / 4 : ℝ) * k * alpha * (h - q) +
        k * (1 + alpha / 4) * (alpha * q / 16 - v) +
        k * alpha * q * (28 - alpha) / 64 := by
    have : 0 ≤ h - q := sub_nonneg.mpr hh
    have : 0 ≤ alpha * q / 16 - v := sub_nonneg.mpr hv
    have : 0 ≤ 28 - alpha := by linarith
    positivity
  nlinarith only [hmargin]

theorem heavy_list_bound (m tau lam : ℝ)
    (hm : 0 < m) (htau : 0 < tau)
    (hlam : lam ≤ tau ^ 2 / 2)
    (hgram : m ^ 2 * tau ^ 2 ≤ m + m ^ 2 * lam) :
    m ≤ 2 / tau ^ 2 := by
  have hslack : 0 ≤ m ^ 2 * (tau ^ 2 / 2 - lam) :=
    mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg m) (sub_nonneg.mpr hlam)
  have hbound : m * tau ^ 2 ≤ 2 := by
    by_contra hn
    have hprod : 0 < m * (m * tau ^ 2 - 2) :=
      mul_pos hm (sub_pos.mpr (lt_of_not_ge hn))
    nlinarith only [hgram, hslack, hprod]
  exact (le_div_iff₀ (sq_pos_of_pos htau)).mpr hbound

theorem excess_domination (p q rho productive : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (ht : 0 ≤ productive)
    (hq : q - rho ≤ productive) :
    p * (q - rho) ≤ productive := by
  by_cases h : q ≤ rho
  · exact le_trans (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos hp (sub_nonpos.mpr h)) ht
  · calc
      p * (q - rho) ≤ 1 * (q - rho) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hp1 (sub_nonneg.mpr (le_of_not_ge h))
      _ ≤ productive := by simpa using hq

theorem productive_characters {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (bad : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred bad]
    (corr : ι → ℝ) (p q rho threshold : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < (s.card : ℝ))
    (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (hthreshold : 0 ≤ threshold)
    (hcorr : ∀ i ∈ s, |corr i| ≤ 1)
    (haverage : q * (s.card : ℝ) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, |corr i|)
    (hbad : ((s.filter bad).card : ℝ) + threshold * (s.card : ℝ) ≤
      rho * (s.card : ℝ)) :
    p * (q - rho) ≤
      ((s.filter fun i => ¬bad i ∧ threshold ≤ |corr i|).card : ℝ) /
        (s.card : ℝ) := by
  classical
  let productive : ι → Prop := fun i => ¬bad i ∧ threshold ≤ |corr i|
  have hpoint (i : ι) (hi : i ∈ s) :
      |corr i| ≤ (if bad i then (1 : ℝ) else 0) +
        (if productive i then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + threshold := by
    by_cases hb : bad i
    · simp only [productive, hb, not_true_eq_false, false_and, if_true, if_false]
      linarith [hcorr i hi]
    · by_cases ht : threshold ≤ |corr i|
      · simp only [productive, hb, ht, not_false_eq_true, true_and, if_true, if_false]
        linarith [hcorr i hi]
      · simp only [productive, hb, ht, not_false_eq_true, true_and, if_false]
        exact le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge ht)
  have hsum : (∑ i ∈ s, |corr i|) ≤
      ((s.filter bad).card : ℝ) +
      ((s.filter productive).card : ℝ) + threshold * (s.card : ℝ) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, ((if bad i then (1 : ℝ) else 0) +
          (if productive i then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + threshold) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum hpoint
      _ = _ := by
        simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_filter, mul_comm]
  have hraw : (q - rho) * (s.card : ℝ) ≤
      ((s.filter productive).card : ℝ) := by
    linarith
  have hquot : q - rho ≤
      ((s.filter productive).card : ℝ) / (s.card : ℝ) :=
    (le_div_iff₀ hn).mpr hraw
  exact excess_domination p q rho _ hp hp1
    (div_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) (le_of_lt hn)) hquot

theorem averaged_decoder_bound {D : Type*} [DecidableEq D]
    (ds : Finset D) (weight p q productive success : D → ℝ)
    (rho b hit : ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ d ∈ ds, 0 ≤ weight d) (hhit : 0 ≤ hit)
    (hdom : ∀ d ∈ ds, p d * (q d - rho) ≤ productive d)
    (hdecoder : ∀ d ∈ ds, productive d * hit ≤ success d)
    (hexcess : b ≤ ∑ d ∈ ds, weight d * (p d * (q d - rho))) :
    b * hit ≤ ∑ d ∈ ds, weight d * success d := by
  calc
    b * hit ≤ (∑ d ∈ ds, weight d * (p d * (q d - rho))) * hit :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hexcess hhit
    _ = ∑ d ∈ ds, weight d * ((p d * (q d - rho)) * hit) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_mul]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro d hd
      ring
    _ ≤ ∑ d ∈ ds, weight d * success d := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro d hd
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (hw d hd)
      exact le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hdom d hd) hhit) (hdecoder d hd)

theorem bias_from_bit_balance (p : ℝ)
    (hp : (1 / 16 : ℝ) ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 15 / 16) :
    |1 - 2 * p| ≤ (7 / 8 : ℝ) := by
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;> linarith

end UpperDecoder

external_assumptions.statement: For every positive retention threshold zeta there are alpha>0, integer r>=1 and ell_0, depending only on zeta, such that for each ell>=ell_0 and then every sufficiently large ambient dimension N, a nonempty family of ell-subspaces with retention at least zeta has density at least alpha in an interval [A,B] with dim A+codim B<=r. Sets of density greater than 1/2 use the whole interval.

claims.natural_statement: Khot-Minzer-Safra TR18-006 revision 2, Theorem 1.12, with the subspace dimension fixed before the ambient-dimension threshold.
Eliminating dummy columns preserves a nonempty affine row/column slice and uniform measure on its image.
lem:stopped-calls, lem:cut-tv and lem:sparse-tv provide the stated common-observation bounds with the enlarged bucket-call counts.
Joint legality and lem:folding make b_y a well-defined normalized functional on all lower-row product generators.
Distinct actual matrices and scalar recursive calls have disjoint random tapes conditional on projected domains and the path through the terminating cut.
Quarter-balanced independent factors imply a 7/8 product-character bias bound and an absolute dimension-independent balance minimum.

For every fixed rational delta in (0,1), there exist an integer q(delta)>=2 and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to nonempty explicit unweighted 2-to-1 games with alphabets [2q],[q], exactly two preimages per right answer, value 1 on satisfiable inputs and value at most delta on unsatisfiable inputs (thm:main).
thm:pcp and thm:repetition supply arbitrarily small constant source value with perfect completeness.
prop:completeness and lem:construction-two-fibers provide one satisfying legal labeling and at-most-two legal projections.
lem:resampling, lem:rank-slice and prop:low-rank turn upper agreement gamma_j into gamma_j/2 low-rank agreement; the lower row requirements depend only on gamma_j.
lem:parity-game, lem:clean-law, lem:reconstruction and prop:clean-bound upper bound that agreement by (1-beta_i*p_0/64)^n_i.

lem:posterior bounds the unconditional probability that at most m adaptively selected children include a projected child by m*beta_i*L_i/(1-beta_i); the two-child bilinear consequence holds without success conditioning.
Root-down row choices, then source repetition, then leaf-up branching give prop:preliminary-soundness; exact-two alphabet padding and rational weight removal give thm:main.

The same local strategies in prop:upper have the stronger all-parameter lower bound b * tau^2/2 * 2^(-r), removing its explicit factor 2^(-ell): per exposure the proportion of nonannihilating output characters with conditional correlation at least rho/2 is at least p_D(q_D-rho), so their average is at least b.

external_assumptions.statement: For every positive retention threshold zeta there are alpha>0, integer r>=1 and ell_0, depending only on zeta, such that for each ell>=ell_0 and then every sufficiently large ambient dimension N, a nonempty family of ell-subspaces with retention at least zeta has density at least alpha in an interval [A,B] with dim A+codim B<=r. Sets of density greater than 1/2 use the whole interval.

The bound is independent of lower row count, source alphabet, branching, and instance size.

routes.retired_because: The initial scaffold left the quantitative productive-character count implicit. R105_GAIN_FULL replaces it with the explicit universal finite-sum obligation U105_EXCESS; the earlier scaffold is not a separate completed proof.

Finite tests, even exhaustive at bounded dimensions, cannot establish the all-parameter upper-decoder interface. The retained finite experiments are adversarial checks only; Theorems A and B and the universal Lean counting theorem supply the argument instead.
